Check that an environment has the requested packages

Source: R/validate_env.R
validate_env.Rd

Checks that an environment exists, and that its installed packages satisfy every package match spec. validate_env() is a query: it never creates or changes an environment. With the micromamba backend, it reports an environment that does not exist without starting a process or installing micromamba. When no micromamba binary is installed, the micromamba backend reads the envs directory of its data directory and the package records in conda-meta/ instead. It never installs micromamba.

Usage

validate_env(
  ...,
  env_name = "condathis-env",
  method = "auto",
  verbose = "silent",
  channels = NULL,
  platform = NULL,
  error = c("cancel", "continue")
)

Arguments

...

Package match specs (MatchSpec strings), unnamed, as in create_env(): character strings or character vectors, in order. With no specs, validate_env() only checks that the environment exists. An installed package satisfies a spec when it matches the name, version, build string and channel of the spec, as Existing environments in create_env() describes. The name match ignores case: "PyYAML" matches pyyaml. A spec without a channel matches a package from channels (see below). A spec with a channel, such as "conda-forge::zlib", matches only a package from that channel. A spec that is not compared, such as "zlib[md5=...]" or "zlib<2.*", never counts as satisfied. These values abort with class condathis_validate_env_invalid_packages:

  • A named argument that validate_env() does not have.

  • A value that is not a character vector.

  • NA or "".

  • A file name that ends in .yml or .yaml.

validate_env() aborts with class condathis_validate_env_positional_env_name when env_name is not given and the last of two or more specs names an existing environment. A spec that condathis cannot read, such as "::", aborts with class condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_name. For the URL of a package file, the class is condathis_parse_match_spec_invalid_url. Both errors also have class condathis_invalid_arg. They abort with error = "continue" too.

env_name

Character string with the environment name. It must be a plain directory name that is valid on Linux, macOS and Windows:

  • Not empty, and not . or ...

  • Not starting with -, and not ending with ..

  • Without path separators, :, #, whitespace, control characters or <>"|?*.

  • Not a Windows device name, such as NUL or COM1 (see Environment names in create_env()).

Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_env_name. Functions that take only names reject an env_path() value with class condathis_env_path_read_only. run(), run_bin(), run_pipeline() and run_step() accept one.

method

Character string naming the backend. "auto" (the default) uses the backend that owns env_name when it exists, and otherwise the first available backend in getOption("condathis.backend_priority") order (see condathis-options). Any name from list_registered_backend_names() selects that backend, and "micromamba" is built in. The name of a backend whose package condathis knows, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package, also selects it. condathis loads the package on first use. It aborts with class condathis_backend_not_installed when the package is not installed. "native" is a deprecated alias for "micromamba" (warns once per session). If you name a backend other than the owner, functions that change the environment abort with class condathis_backend_mismatch. The others warn (condathis_backend_mismatch_warning) and use the owner. An environment found under several backends aborts with condathis_backend_ambiguous_env unless method names one of them. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_method.

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of:

  • "output": show the output of the command and the messages of condathis.

  • "silent": show nothing.

  • "cmd": show the command line.

  • "spinner": show only a spinner.

  • "full": show the command line, the output, and the backend's own log.

TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose (see condathis-conditions). The default is shown in Usage.

The command line shown, the cmd of a result and the messages of condathis show the password and the token of a URL as *****. micromamba does the same (https://user:*****@host/channel, https://host/t/*****/channel). The command still gets them.

channels

NULL (the default) or a non-empty character vector of channel names or URLs. With NULL, a spec without a channel matches a package from any channel. Otherwise, a spec without a channel must match a package from one of channels, compared as in create_env(). A spec with a channel ignores channels. There is no additional_channels: put those channels in channels. Invalid values abort with class condathis_validate_env_invalid_channels.

platform

NULL (the default) or a known conda platform name, such as "linux-64", as platform of create_env() accepts. When given, the packages of the environment must be built for it (noarch packages match any platform). Other values abort with class condathis_validate_env_invalid_platform.

error

Character string. What happens when the environment does not exist or does not have the requested packages: "cancel" (the default) aborts, and "continue" returns FALSE. A backend failure always aborts. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_error.

Value

TRUE, invisibly, when the environment exists and has every requested package. Otherwise, with error = "cancel", it aborts. The class is condathis_validate_env_env_not_found (also condathis_env_not_found) when the environment does not exist. The class is condathis_validate_env_unsatisfied when a spec is not satisfied or the platform differs. The message lists each spec that is not satisfied. With error = "continue", it returns FALSE with two attributes. reason is one of "env_not_found", "platform_mismatch" and "unsatisfied". unsatisfied is a character vector of the specs that are not satisfied (every spec when the environment does not exist). validate_env() reports a platform mismatch before unsatisfied specs. A backend failure aborts with class condathis_validate_env_failed (also condathis_backend_error).

Details

It uses the same check as create_env(overwrite = FALSE). A spec without a channel must match a package from channels, or from any channel when channels is NULL (the default). Given channels = c(channels, additional_channels) of a create_env() call (by default "conda-forge"), validate_env() gives the same answer as that call, with two exceptions. They exist because validate_env() only reads:

  • When method names a backend that does not own the environment, validate_env() warns with class condathis_backend_mismatch_warning and checks the environment with its owner. create_env() aborts with class condathis_backend_mismatch.

  • When a backend cannot tell whether the environment exists, validate_env() still lists its packages, and reports the listing's error if it fails. create_env() aborts with class condathis_backend_probe_failed.

See also

condathis-conditions for every condition class.

Other environments: create_env(), env_exists(), env_path(), get_env_dir(), install_packages(), list_envs(), list_packages(), remove_env()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # A local channel shipped with condathis, with `polyglot`: a
  # dependency-free script that runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.
  channel <- system.file(
    "extdata", "polyglot-channel",
    package = "condathis"
  )
  condathis::create_env(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "polyglot-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  # TRUE, invisibly.
  condathis::validate_env("polyglot", env_name = "polyglot-env")

  # Also TRUE: `polyglot` comes from `channel`, as `create_env()` with
  # the same channels requires.
  condathis::validate_env(
    "polyglot",
    env_name = "polyglot-env",
    channels = channel
  )

  # FALSE, with the reason and the specs that are not satisfied.
  res <- condathis::validate_env(
    "polyglot>=2",
    env_name = "polyglot-env",
    error = "continue"
  )
  print(attr(res, "reason"))
  #> [1] "unsatisfied"
  attr(res, "unsatisfied")
  #> [1] "polyglot>=2"
})
} # }
